title: Kathmandu ↔ Pokhara Tourist Bus
summary: Daily tourist coaches both ways on the Prithvi Highway — reserved seats, hotel-area pickup in Kathmandu, and a lakeside drop in Pokhara.
metaTitle: Kathmandu to Pokhara Tourist Bus | Daily Service
metaDescription: Daily Kathmandu to Pokhara and Pokhara to Kathmandu tourist buses. Schedules, seat classes, prices, and booking with World Touch.
heroAlt: Tourist coach on a mountain highway
overview: The Kathmandu–Pokhara road is how most travelers move between the capital and the lake. World Touch runs daily tourist buses in both directions, aimed at international guests who want a reserved seat, a known pickup, and a coach that is cleaned and crewed for the highway — not a local microbus.

The ride follows the Prithvi Highway beside the Trishuli and Marsyangdi rivers. On a clear day you see Annapurna-range foothills; in monsoon you see green gorges and careful driving. Typical journey time is 7 to 8 hours including a lunch stop, sometimes longer if the highway is slow.
Book with the same Kathmandu desk that handles our treks. If you are starting or finishing a Poon Hill, Mardi, or Annapurna Base Camp trek, we line the bus up with your Pokhara hotel night.
history: We began as a Thamel trekking desk and added the Pokhara coach because guests kept asking for one reliable seat instead of a street-side ticket. The service has run daily in both directions through the main season for years, with sofa and deluxe coaches added as the highway and traveler expectations improved.

notes: Morning departures only — we do not run overnight buses on this route.
A lunch stop is made around Mugling or a similar highway town.
Mountain weather and road works can add time. We would rather arrive late than rush the gorge sections.
Pokhara drop is at a lakeside tourist-bus park; Kathmandu drop is in the Thamel / Sorhakhutte tourist-bus area, with hotel drop on selected coaches.

classes.name: Tourist coach
classes.summary: The everyday reserved-seat bus most travelers choose. Reclining seats, a shared cabin, and a crew that knows the highway stops.
classes.imageAlt: Coach interior with rows of seats

classes.name: Deluxe AC
classes.summary: A newer cabin with stronger air-conditioning, fewer seats, and hotel pickup in Kathmandu on most mornings.
classes.imageAlt: Modern coach on an open road

classes.name: Sofa seat
classes.summary: The most comfortable public option we sell: 1+1 or 2+1 sofa-style seats for guests who want space on a full travel day.
features: Hotel pickup where the coach allows

amenities: Reserved seating — your name is on a seat, not a scramble at the door
Luggage hold for trek duffels; a small bag can stay with you
Lunch stop with time to eat; meals are not included
Air-conditioning on deluxe and sofa coaches
Crew who announce pickup points in English
Simple journey support from our Kathmandu desk if the highway is delayed

policies.title: Booking
policies.detail: Reserve by WhatsApp, email, or the contact form. Same-day seats are sometimes available before 6:00 if the coach is not full — ask, do not assume.

policies.title: Payment
policies.detail: Pay at our Thamel desk, by bank transfer, or in cash on boarding for confirmed bookings. Card payment can be arranged in the office.

policies.title: Cancellation
policies.detail: Free changes up to 24 hours before departure. Later cancellations may keep a seat fee if we cannot resell it.

policies.title: Luggage
policies.detail: One trek duffel and one cabin bag is the usual allowance. Extra cargo needs a check with us first.

policies.title: ID
policies.detail: Carry your passport. Crews may note names against the manifest, especially on deluxe coaches.

faqs.question: How long is the Kathmandu to Pokhara bus?
faqs.answer: Plan on 7 to 8 hours, including a lunch stop. Landslides or traffic near Mugling can make it longer.

faqs.question: Is the tourist bus safe?
faqs.answer: It is the standard way international travelers do this route. We use established highway coaches, morning departures, and crews who drive this road daily. It is still a mountain highway — we do not oversell it as a flight.

faqs.question: Can I book both directions?
faqs.answer: Yes. Most trek guests book Kathmandu to Pokhara before the trek and Pokhara to Kathmandu after.

faqs.question: Do you pick up from my hotel?
faqs.answer: Thamel hotels are covered on morning Kathmandu departures for deluxe and many tourist coaches. Outside Thamel, ask us — we will say clearly if you need to reach the bus park.

faqs.question: Is there Wi-Fi?
faqs.answer: Do not count on it. Mobile data works on much of the highway and drops in the gorges.
